Only one task fits in this session. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Call record_choice for the one to keep. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to break the problem down into smaller, more manageable pieces. You can think of it like looking up a word in a dictionary, only to find the definition uses another word you don't know, forcing you to look up that new word as well. To avoid getting stuck in an infinite loop of lookups, the function must have a base case, which is a simple stopping condition where it no longer calls itself. Once that base case is reached, all the previous function calls resolve one by one, passing their answers back up the chain until the final result is delivered.
